faqs.q: Will my API Key be visible to others?
faqs.a: Absolutely not. Stored keys are heavily encrypted and injected into isolated runtime environments on startup. They are never returned or shown in raw details.

faqs.q: Does each Agent run in isolated containers?
faqs.a: Yes. Each Agent instance runs with isolated container resources. A failure in one instance does not change another instance's runtime state.

faqs.q: Can I bridge with Feishu, Telegram, and Discord?
faqs.a: Yes, completely supported. The network proxy solves all verification, handshake, and structure mappings automatically. You only supply typical Credentials.

faqs.q: Is MyBay suitable for commercial use?
faqs.a: MyBay Open Source can be used commercially under AGPL-3.0-only. Availability, public routing, HTTPS, backups, and recovery remain the self-hosted administrator's responsibility.

faqs.q: How does this differ from building on personal servers?
faqs.a: Self-hosting requires deep DevOps labor, setup layers, reverse routes, and crash logs. MyBay automates all of this to launch safely in under 30 seconds.

categories.name: Quick Start
categories.description: MyBay Open Source purpose and boundaries

items.question: What is MyBay Open Source?
items.answer: MyBay Open Source is a self-hosted AI Agent control plane distributed under AGPL-3.0-only. It is designed for one administrator and manages Hermes Agent through Docker on your own machine. It does not provide cloud accounts, subscription plans, billing, or multi-tenant services.

items.question: How do I install and start it?
items.answer: Use quick-start.sh or quick-start.ps1. The scripts check Docker, create a local .env, generate secure random values, and start Compose services. For manual deployment, replace every security placeholder from .env.example first.

items.question: What data does MyBay Open Source persist?
items.answer: The control plane stores administrator details, instance configuration, encrypted credentials, task records, conversations, chatMessages, chatRuns, chatMessageFeedback, uploaded files, and logs on the host. Structured data is primarily stored in data/mybay.sqlite. Chat history is persistent, not merely held in memory.

items.question: Does all data stay on the local machine?
items.answer: No. The control plane is local-first, but when you configure OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Telegram, Discord, Feishu/Lark, Slack, or another third party, prompts, messages, files, or metadata required for a request may be sent to that service.

items.question: How are API keys and channel tokens stored?
items.answer: Credentials are encrypted locally using ENCRYPTION_KEY, and APIs should not return plaintext to the browser. You must still protect .env, the data directory, backups, and host access, and rotate third-party credentials.

items.question: Why does the control plane need the Docker socket?
items.answer: Instance lifecycle management requires control of the Docker daemon. A MyBay Open Source administrator therefore has high-privilege host-management capability. Do not expose an unprotected control plane directly to the public Internet.

items.question: Does it include model credits or third-party fees?
items.answer: No. You select third-party AI providers and messaging channels and are responsible for their fees, quotas, and terms. MyBay Open Source provides no SaaS SLA and does not guarantee third-party availability.

items.question: How do I diagnose an instance that will not start or open?
items.answer: Review deployment events, container state, and instance logs, then check Docker, image pulls, ports, disk, provider credentials, and reverse proxy settings. Remove passwords, tokens, API keys, domains, and user data before filing an Issue.

terms.title: MyBay Open Source Terms of Use
terms.subtitle: Licensing, deployment, security, and third-party boundaries for the open-source self-hosted software.
terms.suggestionsDesc: Contact the maintainers for licensing or security questions.
terms.footer: MyBay Open Source is offered under AGPL-3.0-only, with a separate commercial license available.

sections.title: 1. Nature of the Software
content: MyBay Open Source is self-hosted open-source software that you deploy, operate, and maintain. It is not a SaaS service operated by the maintainers.
It is provided as-is and does not include cloud accounts, billing, subscription plans, multi-tenant scheduling, or a SaaS service-level agreement.
You are responsible for the server, Docker daemon, network, domains, HTTPS, backups, updates, and capacity.

sections.title: 2. Administrator and Security
content: MyBay Open Source uses a single-administrator model. Use a strong password and secure random secrets, and restrict control-plane network access.
The control plane requires Docker socket access. Treat administrator access as high-privilege host-management capability.
You manage model API keys, channel tokens, .env, SQLite data, and backups.

sections.title: 3. User Content and Third-Party Services
content: You are responsible for prompts, files, configuration, automated tasks, and your use of Agent output, and must comply with applicable law.
You select third-party AI providers and messaging channels and are responsible for their fees, quotas, data processing, and compliance.
Third-party services have their own terms. The project does not guarantee any provider, channel, image registry, or network service.

sections.title: 4. Lawful and Secure Use
content: Do not use the software for unauthorized access, malicious scanning, DDoS, spam, credential theft, or unlawful activity.
Do not remove required notices or violate AGPL-3.0-only source-availability obligations.
Assess Agent tool permissions and automation risks and apply least privilege and auditing.

sections.title: 5. No Service-Level Commitment
content: The project provides no SaaS SLA or guarantee of uptime, response time, data recovery, or third-party connectivity.
Resource limits depend on your host and configuration. Insufficient disk, memory, CPU, or network capacity can cause failures.
AI output can be inaccurate or hallucinatory and requires human review for high-risk decisions.

sections.title: 6. Open-Source License, Commercial License, and Trademarks
content: MyBay Open Source may be used under AGPL-3.0-only, including commercially, subject to its copyleft and source-availability obligations.
Organizations requiring proprietary integration or redistribution without AGPL copyleft obligations may obtain a separate commercial license.
The MyBay name and logos, and third-party brands, are not licensed as trademarks by the AGPL code license.

privacy.title: MyBay Open Source Privacy Notice
privacy.subtitle: Local-first storage, third-party transfers, and self-hosted administrator responsibilities.
privacy.questionsDesc: Report vulnerabilities privately as described in SECURITY.md. Do not place secrets or private data in a public Issue.
privacy.footer: This notice applies to the self-hosted MyBay Open Source.

sections.title: 1. Data Stored Locally
content: MyBay Open Source primarily stores data on the machine you operate. It does not require a MyBay cloud account or cloud database.

Local data may include administrator details, instance configuration, encrypted credentials, task records, conversations, chatMessages, chatRuns, chatMessageFeedback, uploaded files, runtime logs, and audit records.
Structured data is primarily stored in data/mybay.sqlite. MyBay Open Source persists chat history; it is not only held briefly in memory.

sections.title: 2. Local Processing and Security
content: Credentials are encrypted locally using ENCRYPTION_KEY. Host administrators, backup systems, and anyone with Docker daemon access remain inside a high-trust boundary.
The operator is responsible for access control, backups, retention, security updates, and log redaction.
This edition does not include telemetry, cloud billing, or multi-tenant data aggregation.

sections.title: 3. Retention, Backup, and Deletion
content: Retention is controlled by the self-hosted administrator and configured third parties. Define appropriate backup and deletion policies.
Deleting an instance may remove related containers, directories, and records. Verify backups first; the project provides no SaaS recovery commitment.
Removing MyBay Open Source does not erase data already received or retained by third-party providers.

sections.title: 4. Third-Party Services
content: Configured model providers may receive prompts, messages, files, or metadata required to process a request.
Configured channels such as Telegram, Discord, Feishu/Lark, and Slack may receive messages and required metadata.
Third parties apply their own privacy policies, terms, fees, and retention rules.
